newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes lower on Iraqi export news.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes lower on Iraqi export news.

text.p: IPE Brent futures closed lower on Tuesday after news that Iraq is to start exporting oil from the second tranche of its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations in the next seven to 10 days, traders said.
August Brent settled 11 cents down at $17.87 a barrel having tumbled as low as $17.73 on the Iraqi oil export news. July Gas oil closed unchanged at $160.25 a tonne.

Iraqi oil minister Amir Rasheed told reporters in Madrid that Iraq expected to start exporting oil from the second tranche of its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations in the next week to 10 days.
Iraq sold $2 billion worth of oil through the first tranche of the deal which ran through the first six months of the year.
"It's the last thing the bulls wanted," said Nigel Saperia, managing director, of the oil division at Bankers Trust International in London.
Traders said the market would be monitoring news out of the OPEC meeting which begins in Vienna on Wednesday although few expected any change in current OPEC policy.
News that Nigeria was looking to import 33 cargoes of petroleum products due to an acute fuel shortage in the country had little effect on the futures markets. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714
